title: Decode-path latency fingerprinting and Region Failover Inspector
creator: Daniel Ortega
description:
Goal: Create a set of telemetry, SLI derivations, and a dashboard focused on decode-path (post-token-sampling) latency fingerprinting across regions and an inspector view for circuit/capacity failover decisions. This ticket unifies per-token microtrace attribution with an operator-facing Region Failover Inspector that surfaces why traffic moved between regions, the circuit states involved, and which kernel/quantization path contributed to latency spikes.

Why: We frequently see costly tail latency events that are only visible after deep inspection of per-token decode timelines. Operators currently jump between token histograms, per-route SLOs, and region health dashboards. A single, correlated view that ties decode-stage spikes to circuit transitions (open/half-open) and KV/cache hit patterns will reduce MTTR and inform automated failover thresholds.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Telemetry: a stable per-decode-stage latency tag emitted for spans (fetch, kv-prefetch, decode-init, attention-step, kv-commit, emit). Tags must be low-cardinality and correlate to existing request_id and shard_id.
- SLI derivation: p50/p95/p99 for 'decode-path' single-token latency, with quantile rollups per region and per-instance class.
- Dashboard: Region Failover Inspector with panels: decode-fingerprint heatmap, circuit-state timeline, region spillover flow, top contributing kernels by latency, and per-route transient admits.
- Operator actions: quick links from any spike to run a synthetic repro (existing harness) and to toggle a canary failover policy.
- Tests: synthetic traffic experiment demonstrating that inspector correctly attributes a simulated cache-miss-induced p99 spike to the intended region and circuit transition.

Implementation notes: 
- Telemetry schema: emit a new field decode_stage (values: fetch, kv_prefetch, decode_init, attention_step, kv_commit, emit) and decode_latency_ms per stage. Keep field cardinality low; stage names should be stable strings.
- Sampling: sample 1% of requests for full per-stage microtraces, with priority-based amplification to P0 customers and routes flagged as high-sensitivity.
- Storage/backfill: store stage-level aggregates in time-series DB (current metrics pipeline) and microtrace events to the trace store with indexed keys for request_id and region.
- Dashboard build: Grafana / internal console panels. Use heatmap with time buckets and a timeline layer for circuit open/close events. Add a deduplicated list of top kernel/quantization config fingerprints contributing to latency.
- Rollout: staged rollout: feature-flag telemetry -> enable dashboard in staging -> run synthetic validation -> enable default 1% sampling on hosted.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Cost: microtraces can increase ingestion cost. Mitigate by strict sampling and TTL of microtrace events.
- Privacy: microtraces must not contain PII — ensure redaction at emit point.
- False attribution: cross-region queues may skew attribution; include sequence-aware correlation keys and test under multi-region synthetic loads.

Notes on compatibility: Should interoperate with Dedicated and Private collectors — use same low-cardinality decode_stage and map collector-specific instance identifiers to a canonical instance_id.

testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for stage tags and latency emission. 2) End-to-end synthetic: create a staging lane that injects 0.5% cache-miss traffic and validate decode-stage attribution. 3) Load test: run 10k rps synthetic across two regions and verify sampling overhead and dashboard correctness.
operational_playbook: If the inspector shows a region spillover with circuit open: 1) run repro via dashboard CTA, 2) check kernel fingerprint panel to choose fallback kernel, 3) temporarily enable canary failover to target region, 4) file incident note with investigator and timeline.
notes: Keep names stable: decode_stage and kernel_fingerprint_id must not change without a migration plan. Sync with Dedicated team for instance_id mapping before launch.
